backlog.spec: Retune only the RandomForest member: set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF = 3, MAX_FEATURES = 'sqrt', and N_TREES = 600, leaving LightGBM, the features and the rank-average blend untouched. Rationale: with max_features=0.3 of roughly 2250 columns each split scans ~675 features and leaves hold a single molecule, so the forest produces spiky, over-confident probabilities; AUROC rewards well-ordered graded scores, so coarser leaves give smoother ranks, and a smaller feature fraction with more trees increases tree diversity, which is the usual way a forest gains on wide sparse-plus-dense matrices. Keep random_state=seed and n_jobs=-1.
backlog.title: Smoother forest: larger leaves and sqrt feature fraction

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, after fitting the RF and LightGBM models, fit a CatBoostClassifier(iterations=600, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, rsm=0.1, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0) on the same X_train, y. Return the equal-weight mean of the three scaled_rank prediction vectors (RF, LightGBM, CatBoost) instead of the two-way mean. If the job gets close to the 10-minute limit, reduce iterations to 400. No other changes.
backlog.title: Add CatBoost as a third blend member

backlog.spec: Change only the LGBMClassifier settings to: n_estimators=1000, learning_rate=0.02, num_leaves=8, min_child_samples=10, colsample_bytree=0.2, subsample=0.7, subsample_freq=1, reg_lambda=5.0, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1. Leave the RF and the rank-average blend untouched.
backlog.title: Stronger regularized LightGBM: more trees, lower rate, row subsampling

backlog.spec: Add an sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=500, max_features=0.2, min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed) fitted on the same X_train, y as a third model. Return the equal-weight mean of scaled_rank of the RF, LightGBM and ExtraTrees class-1 probabilities. Keep the existing RF and LightGBM settings as they are.
backlog.title: Replace RandomForest with ExtraTrees plus keep RF (three-way blend)

backlog.spec: After computing the blended rank score for the test molecules, post-process it once: build Morgan radius-2 2048-bit fingerprints for the test molecules, compute the test-test Tanimoto similarity matrix, and for each test molecule replace its score by 0.75 * own score + 0.25 * (similarity-weighted mean of the scores of its 5 most similar other test molecules, weights = similarity cubed, falling back to the own score if the top similarity is below 0.2). Return the smoothed vector. Rationale: this is a transductive consistency prior saying close analogues should receive close scores, it uses no test labels, and it damps idiosyncratic single-molecule errors from the tree members; keep the mixing weight and k as module-level constants and leave training completely unchanged.
backlog.title: Smooth final predictions over Tanimoto neighbours of the test set

backlog.spec: Instead of fitting both models on the single concatenated matrix, build two views inside fit_predict: view F = Morgan bits only (the first N_BITS columns), view D = the 11 hand descriptors plus the clipped full RDKit descriptor block. Fit four models: RF on F, RF on D, LightGBM on F, LightGBM on D, each with the current hyperparameters (for the D view use max_features='sqrt' in the RF and colsample_bytree=0.5 in LightGBM, because D has only about 230 columns). Return the mean of scaled_rank over the four prediction vectors. The reason: in the concatenated matrix the 2048 sparse bits dilute the per-split sampling of the informative descriptors.
backlog.title: Separate feature views: fingerprint model and descriptor model

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, split the feature matrix into the Morgan bit block and the descriptor blocks. Fit sklearn.decomposition.TruncatedSVD(n_components=64, random_state=seed) on the training Morgan block only, transform both train and test, and feed [SVD64 | 11 physchem | clipped descList] to the unchanged RF and LightGBM members with the unchanged rank-average blend. Rationale: the SVD components are dense linear combinations of correlated substructure bits, so a single tree split on a component can express a structural concept that otherwise needs many sparse splits, and the 64-column block no longer swamps the descriptor columns during feature subsampling. Fit the SVD on train only to keep the fold honest.
backlog.title: Replace raw fingerprint bits with a truncated-SVD embedding

backlog.spec: Make no functional change: the only edit is to add a short comment line near the Settings block (for example '# replicate run: no functional change'). The purpose is a third measurement of the current RF+LightGBM blend with full descList descriptors, whose two existing runs differ by ~0.01 (twice the stated noise sd), so the incumbent mean is poorly pinned down. Keep fit_predict, the feature pipeline, both members and the equal-weight rank average exactly as they are, and keep using the seed argument for both estimators. This slot buys a tighter baseline so that later single-run deltas of 0.005-0.01 can be judged.
backlog.title: Replicate the incumbent to firm up the baseline

backlog.spec: In featurize(), in addition to the existing binary Morgan bits, append a count-based Morgan fingerprint (radius 2, fpSize 2048) obtained with gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy(mol) from the same rdFingerprintGenerator Morgan generator. Clip counts at 15 and store as float32. Keep everything else (the 11 hand descriptors, the full RDKit descriptor block, RF + LightGBM rank-average) unchanged. The purpose is to let the trees split on how many times a substructure occurs, not only on presence.
backlog.title: Add count-based Morgan fingerprint block

backlog.spec: Keep both members and the feature pipeline unchanged but replace the equal-weight rank average with a weighted one: return 0.35 * scaled_rank(rf_prob) + 0.65 * scaled_rank(gb_prob). Expose the weight as a module-level constant W_GB = 0.65 so it is easy to re-tune later. Rationale: the descriptor block (full descList, clipped) is dense and continuous, which boosting exploits better than a fingerprint-oriented random forest, so the optimal mixture is probably not 50/50; the forest is kept at non-trivial weight because it decorrelates the boosting errors. Change nothing else, and keep passing seed to both estimators.
backlog.title: Tune the blend weight toward LightGBM

memo: Helped: the RF+LightGBM blend (0.1194 vs baseline ~0.1361) and appending RDKit descriptors (11 physchem 0.1040; full descList 0.0944 and 0.0842, incumbent mean_adjusted 0.0893 over 2 runs). Descriptors drive the gain. Did not help: other fingerprint swaps or additions (atom-pair 0.0949, MACCS 0.0921, Morgan counts 0.0940, BRICS 0.0938), model swaps (XGBoost 0.1041, CatBoost 0.0950, ExtraTrees 0.0948, SVC 0.1255), LightGBM variants (DART 0.0967, regularized 0.0958, monotone 0.0942), and extra members like LR or MLP. Tanimoto kNN (0.0884), label spreading (0.0896), torsion counts (0.0902) and LR stacking (0.0900) were within noise. The two incumbent runs differ by about 0.01, twice the noise sd of ~0.0049, so single-run deltas under 0.01 are unreliable. Next: replicate the incumbent and the kNN variant to firm up the baseline. Tune blend weights and tree hyperparameters on the descriptors. Try fewer fingerprint bits. Avoid more fingerprint swaps, kernel models and model-family swaps.
